concepts.label: Indexing (Couchbase Lite)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - CBL indexes are a local, embedded (SQLite-backed) mechanism created via API/config objects, not a server-side GSI; do NOT reuse server/'s index-state concept

concepts.label: Value Index
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - basic property index created via ValueIndexConfiguration or IndexBuilder.valueIndex

concepts.label: Partial Index
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - index restricted by a WHERE clause; selection governed by SQLite's partial-index optimizer rules, not a Couchbase-server concept

concepts.label: Partial Full-Text Index
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - unlike partial value indexes, always used when match() is invoked regardless of the optimizer

concepts.label: Array Index
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - indexes values within a nested array to make UNNEST queries more efficient; no analogue in server/'s GSI index types documented so far

relations.subject: cbl:array-index

relations.subject: cbl:indexing
relations.evidence: You can use SQL++ or QueryBuilder syntaxes to create an index

cross_product_finding: Indexing here is a purely local, embedded concept (SQLite-backed), with none of server/'s GSI machinery (no index-service, no index-state lifecycle enum, no CREATE INDEX statement executed as a cluster operation - confirmed later by query-n1ql-mobile-server-diffs.md, which states 'CREATE INDEX ... Not Supported' for SQL++ for Mobile). Indexes are created only through platform API/config objects (ValueIndexConfiguration, IndexBuilder, ArrayIndexConfiguration, FullTextIndexConfiguration), never through a SQL++ statement string. Partial indexes are gated by SQLite's own query-optimizer rules (explicitly cited from sqlite.org), which is a mechanism with no counterpart in server/'s or Capella's access-control or index vocabularies. Array indexing is a CBL-specific optimization for UNNEST that also has no server/ or Capella analogue found so far.
notable_absence: No index-state lifecycle enum (comparable to server/'s GSI index-state) is documented on this page - index creation/deletion via the API appears synchronous from the developer's point of view, with no 'building/online/deferred' style states described.
